newsitem.title: USA: Texas Pacific to buy Belden & Blake.
newsitem.headline: Texas Pacific to buy Belden & Blake.

text.p: Belden & Blake Co., an oil and gas exploration and production company, announced Monday it would be bought by Texas Pacific Group for $315 million in cash, prompting a surge in its stock.

Belden & Blake stock jumped $4.875, or 23 percent, to $25.625 in early afternoon trading, making it one of Nasdaq's biggest percentage gainers. Trading in the stock was halted for about 1-1/2 hours for the announcement of the acquisition.

Texas Pacific, a private investment partnership, will pay $27 a share, or $305.1 million, for 11.3 million shares of common stock, plus $10 million for some stock options held by Belden employees and directors, Belden Chief Financial Officer Ronald Huff said in a telephone interview.

The North Canton, Ohio-based company's chairman, Henry Belden, and its president, Max Mardick, will retire from Belden after the deal is completed, the company said. It said the two men would be expected to serve on the new Texas Pacific subsidiary's board.
Texas Pacific said it expected to name Ronald Clements, now Belden's senior vice president of exploration and production, as the new chief executive officer and to name Huff as president.
The deal is subject to shareholder and regulatory approval, Belden said.

North Canton, Ohio-based Belden operates in the Appalachian, Michigan and Illinois oil basins, an area which includes Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia, Kentucky and Michigan. The company, founded in 1942, has more than 600 employees, according to Huff.
As of Dec. 31, 1996, Belden owned interests in more than 7,700 productive oil and gas wells with proved reserves totalling more than 288 billion cubic feet of gas and 7.4 million barrels of oil.
The company made $14.8 million in profits on revenues of $153.2 million in 1996.

Texas Pacific, based in San Francisco and Fort Worth, Texas, made its first investment in the oil and gas industry in December 1995, when it bought a stake in Denbury Resources Inc., a Dallas-based energy exploration and production company.

Texas Pacific said the partnership and its principals have made significant investments in various industries, including airlines, health care, motorcycles, telecommunications, food wine, entertainment and waste management.
